source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

historical_synonyms_documented: Quercus texana of authors, not Buckley

morphology_documented.habit: Small tree, usually to 10 m, rarely taller
morphology_documented.leaves: Alternate simple deciduous (genus); finely and deeply lobed compared with Q. shumardii; bristle-bearing red-oak group
morphology_documented.flowers: Spring; monoecious with male catkins and short female spikes (genus)
morphology_documented.habitat: Limestone outcrops, slopes and stream bottoms, rarely sandy ground

source_scope_note: Species vs genus/key-level characters distinguished in text; no undocumented characters inferred.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: Important: 1999 source says name Q. texana previously misapplied and restricts true Q. texana to more easterly taxa
Reports narrow hybridization belt with Q. shumardii, including toward Bexar County; some individuals cannot be distinguished confidently
Flora questions rank in relation to Q. shumardii, retain provenance
preservation: Additive research record, existing species cards, original media, credits and galleries unchanged
